Estimate a correction on each imputation and pool it

Source: R/recalibrate.R
mm_recal_mi.Rd

Scoring a sample by multiple imputation produces one linear predictor per imputation per row, so there are several estimates of the correction and they have to be combined. Getting the pooling wrong is invisible: the point estimate is right either way and only the interval is too narrow.

Usage

mm_recal_mi(
  lp_mat,
  y,
  cluster = NULL,
  form = c("intercept", "two-parameter"),
  positive = NULL
)

Arguments

lp_mat

An n by m matrix of linear predictors, one column per imputation, rows in one consistent order.

y

The outcome, length n, in that same row order.

cluster

An identifier for rows that are not independent, or NULL.

form

"intercept" for the constant alone, "two-parameter" for a + b * lp.

positive

The level that means the event.

Value

A list: a, b, se_a, se_b, b_p, n, n_clusters, m, fmi_a, fmi_b, per_imputation, and a one-line reason.

Details

This package fits on complete rows and has no imputation of its own, so lp_mat comes from imputing elsewhere and scoring each completed data set.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 9)
fit <- suppressWarnings(mm_model(
  mm_project("recal", "event", c("age", "bmi"),
             positive_class = 1, cohort = cohort), cohort))
lp <- as.numeric(fit$fit$linear.predictors)
# Two "imputations" standing in for a real set, to show the shape.
mm_recal_mi(cbind(lp, lp + 0.05), cohort$event, positive = 1)$a
#> [1] -0.025
